record.name: Nina Mamužić
record.title: Senior Research Associate
record.bio: Nina Mamužić completed her undergraduate and master's studies in Food Technology at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2005 and 2007 respectively. She obtained her PhD in 2013 from the same institution, with a dissertation on the microencapsulation of lipid-rich plant extracts in protein-polysaccharide carriers. She joined the Department of Food Preservation Engineering as a Research Associate in 2014 and was promoted to Senior Research Associate in 2020. Her group focuses on spray-drying and freeze-drying encapsulation of oxidation-sensitive lipids, wall material formulation, and in vitro digestion modelling. She teaches elective courses in food packaging and functional food technology at the master's level. The laboratory is equipped with a Büchi B-290 spray dryer, a TA Instruments DSC, HPLC with fluorescence detection, a Malvern Zetasizer, and a Rancimat unit for accelerated oxidation testing.

record.industry_experience: Vesna Mitrović collaborated with a Novi Sad-based cold-pressing facility (Vojvodinaoleum d.o.o., a fictitious company) on a short-term contract to characterise their hemp oil batches for composition consistency and primary oxidation markers. This engagement ran from 2017 to 2018 and informed the selection of raw material specifications used in subsequent academic studies.
record.notes: Vesna Mitrović has expressed interest in partnerships with companies at NTP Novi Sad that produce plant-based food supplements, functional dairy, or bakery ingredients, particularly those seeking to add omega-3 claims to their products. She is not currently on sabbatical and is available for collaborative discussions. Her laboratory capacity for spray drying is shared with two other research groups, so large-scale contract work would require scheduling coordination.
